source.title: 7. Diabetes Technology: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
source.citation: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee for Diabetes. 7. Diabetes technology: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026. Diabetes Care 2026;49(Suppl. 1):S150–S165.

atoms.canonical_statement: The ADA recommends offering diabetes devices to people with diabetes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The ADA recommends offering diabetes devices to people with diabetes.

atoms.canonical_statement: Device type and selection should be individualized to the person’s needs, circumstances, preferences, and skill level; caregiver skills and preferences are integral when another person manages some or all diabetes care.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Device type and selection should be individualized to the person’s needs, circumstances, preferences, and skill level; caregiver skills and preferences are integral when another person manages some or all diabetes care.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: When prescribing CGM, people with diabetes and caregivers should receive initial and ongoing training and education suited to their circumstances.

atoms.canonical_statement: People with diabetes should receive BGM devices according to their circumstances, preferences, and treatment.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: People with diabetes should receive BGM devices according to their circumstances, preferences, and treatment.

atoms.canonical_statement: People using CGM must also have access to BGM at all times.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: People using CGM must also have access to BGM at all times.

atoms.canonical_statement: People taking insulin and using BGM should check glucose when appropriate to their insulin therapy, including around meals, sleep, exercise, suspected hypo- or hyperglycemia, treatment of low glucose, and critical tasks such as driving.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: People taking insulin and using BGM should check glucose when appropriate to their insulin therapy, including around meals, sleep, exercise, suspected hypo- or hyperglycemia, treatment of low glucose, and critical tasks such as driving.

atoms.canonical_statement: Health care professionals should account for differences in blood glucose meter accuracy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Health care professionals should account for differences in blood glucose meter accuracy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Only meters approved by the FDA or comparable regulators with proven accuracy should be used, with unexpired strips from a licensed source and proper storage.

atoms.canonical_statement: Although BGM has not consistently produced clinically significant A1C reductions in people on noninsulin therapies, it may help when meals, activity, or medications are being modified within a treatment-adjustment program.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: CGM is recommended at diabetes onset and thereafter for children, adolescents, and adults receiving insulin therapy.

atoms.canonical_statement: CGM is recommended for people using noninsulin therapies that can cause hypoglycemia.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: CGM is recommended for people using noninsulin therapies that can cause hypoglycemia.

atoms.canonical_statement: CGM is recommended with any diabetes treatment when CGM helps management.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: CGM is recommended with any diabetes treatment when CGM helps management.

atoms.canonical_statement: The CGM device and method should be selected according to the individual’s circumstances, preferences, and needs.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The CGM device and method should be selected according to the individual’s circumstances, preferences, and needs.

atoms.canonical_statement: People on insulin therapy should use CGM as close to daily as possible for maximal benefit.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: People on insulin therapy should use CGM as close to daily as possible for maximal benefit.

atoms.canonical_statement: People with diabetes should have uninterrupted access to CGM supplies to minimize gaps in use.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: People with diabetes should have uninterrupted access to CGM supplies to minimize gaps in use.

atoms.canonical_statement: During pregnancy with type 1 diabetes, CGM can help achieve time-in-range and time-above-range goals.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: During pregnancy with type 1 diabetes, CGM can help achieve the A1C goal.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: CGM may be beneficial for other types of diabetes in pregnancy.

atoms.canonical_statement: Irritant or allergic skin reactions related to devices should be assessed and addressed to support successful use.

atoms.canonical_statement: People wearing CGM devices should be educated about substances and other factors that may interfere with accuracy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: People wearing CGM devices should be educated about substances and other factors that may interfere with accuracy.

atoms.canonical_statement: For people with insulin-requiring diabetes using MDI, insulin pens are preferred in most cases.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: For people with insulin-requiring diabetes using MDI, insulin pens are preferred in most cases.

atoms.canonical_statement: Insulin syringes remain an option based on person or caregiver preference, insulin formulation and vial availability, dosing needs, cost, and self-management capability.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Insulin syringes remain an option based on person or caregiver preference, insulin formulation and vial availability, dosing needs, cost, and self-management capability.

atoms.canonical_statement: Insulin pens or injection aids are recommended for dexterity or vision impairment or when chosen through shared decision-making to improve accurate insulin dosing and administration.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Insulin pens or injection aids are recommended for dexterity or vision impairment or when chosen through shared decision-making to improve accurate insulin dosing and administration.

atoms.canonical_statement: Connected insulin pens should be offered when appropriate to people with diabetes taking multiple daily insulin injections.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Connected insulin pens should be offered when appropriate to people with diabetes taking multiple daily insulin injections.

atoms.canonical_statement: FDA-approved insulin dose calculators or decision-support systems may help calculate insulin doses.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: FDA-approved insulin dose calculators or decision-support systems may help calculate insulin doses.

atoms.canonical_statement: AID is the preferred insulin delivery method over MDI, CSII, and sensor-augmented pumps for people with type 1 diabetes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: AID is the preferred insulin delivery method over MDI, CSII, and sensor-augmented pumps for people with type 1 diabetes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: AID is the preferred insulin delivery method over MDI, CSII, and sensor-augmented pumps for adults with type 2 diabetes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Choice of AID system should be based on the individual’s circumstances, preferences, and needs.

atoms.canonical_statement: People who have been using CSII or AID should have continued access across third-party payors.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: People who have been using CSII or AID should have continued access across third-party payors.
